short: ASR-teacher labels (M02) replaced transcribed-data alignment targets; standard: LRS2 parity holds, but effects differ across datasets, one WER each, and distillation is not isolated.
position: The paper [@afouras2020asr] changes the training labels (M02): an audio-only ASR teacher supplies transcripts and frame posteriors for untranscribed video. Earlier lip readers took audio-derived frame targets only from transcribed data [@sari2018avicar]; none of 77 matches ASR labels or distillation (pattern match, Appendix). On LRS2 the no-label arm matches ground truth (58.2% against 58.5%, Table 3), which supports the authors' parity claim. It stays standard, not ahead: the label effect differs across datasets (0.3 points on LRS2, 3.2 on LRS3), each one WER with no run count, and no row separates distillation from CTC on ASR labels. The public-data state-of-the-art claim (M12) rests on 0.3- and 0.4-point margins over the [concurrent] Conv-seq2seq [@zhang2019convseq2seq] (inference).
